precepts.text: The sceptre shall not depart from Judah: the kingship shall not depart from Judah; nor a lawgiver from between his feet: that is the priesthood, letting you know Christ would come from the rod; there is no immaculate anything, that is Egyptian and Babylonian make believe; until Shiloh come: that is the Messiah, Christ; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.
precepts.point: In that day shall ye call every man his neighbour under the vine and under the fig tree: that is in the kingdom.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

precepts.why:
The priesthood and the kingship that Christ fulfilled go back to Jacob's blessing on Judah: “The sceptre shall not depart from Judah”: the kingship shall not depart from Judah. “nor a lawgiver from between his feet”: that is the priesthood, and what is between a man's feet is his rod. It shows Christ would come from the rod. There is no immaculate anything; that is make-believe, Egyptian and Babylonian fairy tales. “until Shiloh come”: that is the Messiah, Christ. “and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.”

Matthew 1 traces the line through the captivity. “And after they were brought to Babylon, Jechonias begat Salathiel; and Salathiel begat Zorobabel”, and so down to “Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.” That is the Branch coming out of Zerubbabel, the governor who stood with Joshua the high priest.

In the sit-down with Captain Matathias and Captain Galiah, the dude with that stupid hat argued there was a curse on Jechonias that no one of his seed would sit as king, so the genealogy is ruled out. But after Babylon came in, that was it: Zedekiah was taken away and his sons were killed, and no king sat on the throne in Israel. There was no king in the time of Christ. When he came, the people loved him so much that they wanted to “take him by force, to make him a king”, and “he departed again into a mountain himself alone.” By the prophets, there would be no more king until Christ returns: the sceptre waits for Shiloh.

precepts.text: The sceptre shall not depart from Judah: the kingship. Nor a lawgiver from between his feet, meaning sperm; your loins is between your feet. That let you know there is no immaculate conception. Until Shiloh come: until Christ comes. And unto him shall the gathering of the people be: he's the only one that can gather all 12 tribes together.
precepts.point: Definition read in class: perdition primarily refers to eternal damnation or the state of spiritual ruin and hell, originating from the Latin word perdere, meaning to destroy or to lose. The noun is often used to describe the fate of the wicked or the absolute loss of one's soul. In Christian theology it signifies the final loss of salvation and the unending punishment of a soul in the afterlife.

note.label: Drowning in Sin & Perdition

precepts.why:
Paul beseeches the brethren “by the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ, and by our gathering together unto him.” That “him” is Christ, and Genesis 49:10 shows why: “unto him shall the gathering of the people be.” He is the only one who can gather all twelve tribes together. When people on earth say they are the ones Christ is using to gather the twelve tribes, don't listen to that.

Jacob's blessing lays it out. “The sceptre shall not depart from Judah”: the sceptre is the kingship. “nor a lawgiver from between his feet”: between the feet means the loins, the seed. The lawgiver comes out of Judah's loins, which shows there is no immaculate conception. “until Shiloh come”: until Christ comes.

That is why Paul tells them “be not soon shaken in mind, or be troubled.” In his time many were running around saying the resurrection had come and gone already. Paul reminds them not to let anyone deceive them; Christ had not returned, and the gathering belongs to him alone, when he comes.

precepts.text: They have taken crafty counsel against thy people, and consulted against thy hidden ones. The same words the record used: a people now hidden.
precepts.point: The blessings of thy father have prevailed above the blessings of my progenitors: what God promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob was not yet fulfilled in their day, but Joseph ruled all Egypt. Canaan wasn't ours yet, and Joseph already had the crown.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.why:
Jacob called his sons together in Egypt to tell them “that which shall befall you in the last days,” and highlight those last words: the last days. Of Joseph he said, “Joseph is a fruitful bough, even a fruitful bough by a well; whose branches run over the wall.” By a well: they would live by the waters, on islands, in the last days. The walls are forts like El Morro, built by the Spanish to keep the other European powers out of places like Puerto Rico. “The archers have sorely grieved him, and shot at him, and hated him”: the conquistadors sorely grieved him. “But his bow abode in strength.”

The Spaniards' own records, gathered in the book Lost Tribes and Promised Land, bear this out. Duran found Judaic customs in the old Aztec religion, unleavened bread on certain days and bathing for purification, and came to believe the Indians descended from the lost tribes of Israel. In 1644 an Indian guide named Francisco declared that his countrymen would be avenged upon the Spaniards in time by means of a people now hidden. Montesinos, a Judaizer imprisoned by the Inquisition, was reciting the formula of the New World Marranos, Blessed be the name of the Lord, who has not made me an idolater, a barbarian, a negro, an Indian, when he stopped and told himself, Those Indians, they are Hebrews. Indians later came to Antonio de Montesinos and recited the Shema in Hebrew, Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is one, and told him they were of the tribe of Reuben, and that the tribe of Joseph lived on an island nearby. That is Puerto Rico, with Manasseh in Cuba.

That people now hidden is Judah, and the Psalm uses the same words the record used: “They have taken crafty counsel against thy people, and consulted against thy hidden ones.” Israel is God's hidden people, and the nations have taken crafty counsel against them. The Spaniards' records, which they collected and kept, testify of the hidden ones the Bible speaks of.

precepts.text: The kingdom and dominion, and the greatness of the kingdom under the whole heaven, shall be given to the people of the saints of the Most High: that's the whole earth, exactly what the tablets said.
precepts.point: The blessings of thy father have prevailed above the blessings of my progenitors: what God promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob was not yet fulfilled in their day, but Joseph ruled all Egypt. Canaan wasn't ours yet, and Joseph already had the crown.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.why:
The records of the Spanish explorers tell what the Indians' own sorcerers had said: that the God of these children of Israel is the true God, that everything inscribed on their tablets is true, that at the end of days they will be lords of all the nations of the earth, and that after one nation comes bringing many things to that land, these children of Israel will go forth from where they are and reign over the whole earth as they once did. That is what the nations don't want.

Daniel says the very same thing: “And the kingdom and dominion, and the greatness of the kingdom under the whole heaven, shall be given to the people of the saints of the most High, whose kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions shall serve and obey him.” Under the whole heaven is the whole earth, exactly what the tablets said.

This is the blessing Jacob put on Joseph's head in Genesis 49. “The blessings of thy father have prevailed above the blessings of my progenitors”: what God promised to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob was not yet fulfilled in their day, Canaan was not yet theirs, but Joseph already ruled all Egypt. Joseph wore the crown before the kingdom came, a picture of the dominion that will be given to the saints in the last days.

precepts.text: Moses blessed the twelve tribes before his death. Of Joseph he said, blessed of the Lord be his land: the precious things of heaven, the deep that coucheth beneath, the precious fruits brought forth by the sun and the precious things put forth by the moon; there are things on Cuba and Puerto Rico that only come forth by the moon. The goodwill of him that dwelt in the bush: that's Christ. His horns are like the horns of unicorns, meaning the rhinoceros: with them he shall push the people together to the ends of the earth; and they are the ten thousands of Ephraim, and they are the thousands of Manasseh. Ephraim and Manasseh were used instrumentally by God to push the ten tribes from the eastern hemisphere to the western hemisphere.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.why:
“And this is the blessing, wherewith Moses the man of God blessed the children of Israel before his death.” Moses blessed the twelve tribes before he died, and his blessing of Joseph matches Jacob's in Genesis 49.

“And of Joseph he said, Blessed of the Lord be his land, for the precious things of heaven, for the dew, and for the deep that coucheth beneath.” That is Jacob's “blessings of heaven above, blessings of the deep that lieth under”: good climate and good weather, and the fish and treasures beneath the waters. “And for the precious fruits brought forth by the sun, and for the precious things put forth by the moon”: there are things on Cuba and Puerto Rico that only come forth by the moon, like the coquí frog that comes out in the time of the moon.

“and for the good will of him that dwelt in the bush”: that is Christ, whose spirit was in the bush. “let the blessing come upon the head of Joseph, and upon the top of the head of him that was separated from his brethren,” just as Jacob said the blessings “shall be on the head of Joseph, and on the crown of the head of him that was separate from his brethren.”

“His glory is like the firstling of his bullock”: that is Ephraim. “and his horns are like the horns of unicorns,” meaning the rhinoceros: “with them he shall push the people together to the ends of the earth: and they are the ten thousands of Ephraim, and they are the thousands of Manasseh.” That is very important. Ephraim and Manasseh were used instrumentally by God to push the ten tribes from the eastern hemisphere to the western hemisphere.

precepts.why:
Ezra explains how Ephraim and Manasseh pushed the people “to the ends of the earth”: “Those are the ten tribes, which were carried away prisoners out of their own land in the time of Osea the king, whom Salmanasar the king of Assyria led away captive, and he carried them over the waters, and so came they into another land.”

“But they took this counsel among themselves, that they would leave the multitude of the heathen, and go forth into a further country, where never mankind dwelt,” “That they might there keep their statutes, which they never kept in their own land.” “And they entered into Euphrates by the narrow places of the river.” “For the most High then shewed signs for them, and held still the flood, till they were passed over.”

“For through that country there was a great way to go, namely, of a year and a half: and the same region is called Arsareth.” It took a year and a half to travel, and that region called Arsareth is the land now called America. That is how Joseph became the fruitful bough by a well in the western hemisphere, whose branches run over the wall.

“They shall walk after the Lord: he shall roar like a lion: when he shall roar, then the children shall tremble from the west.” The children of Israel are in the west when the Lord roars.

How did they get to the west? Deuteronomy 33:17 and 2 Esdras 13 just told you. Ephraim and Manasseh, with the horns of the unicorn, pushed the people together to the ends of the earth, and the ten tribes went a year and a half's journey into the region called Arsareth.

So the blessing of Joseph in Genesis 49, “in the last days,” is a blessing on a people in the western hemisphere, by the waters, on the islands. It is from the west that the children will tremble and come when the Lord roars.

“Ephraim, he hath mixed himself among the people; Ephraim is a cake not turned.” Some like to say that is not talking about mixing with other races. It is, and 1 Esdras 8:70 is the precept for it.

Ephraim today is like that: some are very light, extremely light, some able to pass for Esau, because they mixed with Esau; others who did not mix are very dark.

“Strangers have devoured his strength, and he knoweth it not”: the white man has devoured Ephraim's strength, and Ephraim does not realize it. “yea, gray hairs are here and there upon him, yet he knoweth not”: Ephraim grows old and does not know his own history. The fruitful bough of Genesis 49, blessed above his brethren, has been mixed and devoured and has forgotten who he is.

The holy seed is mixed: that is the word. Israel married the daughters of the strange people of the land, and the scripture calls it iniquity. There is the precept for the mixing.

So when Hosea says Ephraim is “a cake not turned,” it is describing what that mixing produced: part of Ephraim very light from mixing with Esau, and part very dark because they did not mix.

precepts.why:
“As for Ephraim, their glory shall fly away like a bird, from the birth, and from the womb, and from the conception.” “Though they bring up their children, yet will I bereave them.”

“Ephraim, as I saw Tyrus, is planted in a pleasant place”: that pleasant place is what Moses and Jacob spoke of, the islands, the fruitful bough by a well. “but Ephraim shall bring forth his children to the murderer.” Ephraim would willingly give their children over to improve the race, as the doctrine of la raza taught: wanting children with straight hair, light skin and lighter eyes, not the nappy hair. That is what the Bible said Ephraim would do.

“Give them, O Lord: what wilt thou give? give them a miscarrying womb and dry breasts.” God says he will deal himself with the seed of the oppressor mixed in; so don't worry about it, brothers, just teach. “Ephraim is smitten, their root is dried up, they shall bear no fruit: yea, though they bring forth, yet will I slay even the beloved fruit of their womb.”

Joseph was blessed with “blessings of the breasts, and of the womb.” When Ephraim mixed with the murderer, that same blessing was turned: a miscarrying womb and dry breasts. The root of the fruitful bough is dried up because of the mixing.

note.label: The Superiority of the Chosen People

precepts.why:
“Judah is a lion’s whelp.” He was a young lion in the 1960s, and after that he fell and became the old lion: “who shall rouse him up?” Then: “The sceptre shall not depart from Judah, nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh come; and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.” Shiloh is Christ, and unto him, and to Judah, shall the gathering of the people be. Judah is the essential tribe to bring all twelve tribes together, the very liberation the 1969 hearings feared, which is why they said they had to destroy Judah among the African American community: education, revised Bibles, contraception, autism, using all they can to destroy these negroes.

Deuteronomy 33:7 is Moses’ blessing on the same tribe: “And this is the blessing of Judah: and he said, Hear, Lord, the voice of Judah, and bring him unto his people: let his hands be sufficient for him; and be thou an help to him from his enemies.” Bring Judah unto his people on an international scale: bring Judah to all the tribes, so that we can get out of here. Judah, Benjamin and Levi are giving these devils hell, and all twelve tribes are going to rise up together and bring hell to this kingdom.

It is already happening. A sister in Papua New Guinea wrote to one of our groups that her people thought they were free of colonization after independence in 1975, but religion still holds them colonized, enslaved, trapped and in poverty. Her answer was to go back to the origins of the Bible, obey it, and see what the Lord can do for their country: Genesis 49:8-12, and to listen to the tribe of Judah, who holds the sceptre, whom all tribes shall praise. Our people there know Judah has been sent to revive them.

That is why Judah in America is kept down. Every other tribe, in Jamaica, in Africa, in Europe, Levi speaking six languages, is better educated than Judah here. If Judah knew five or six languages, this thing would be over quickly. So the schools are dumbed down for Judah, while the blessing stands: the Lord will hear Judah’s voice, bring him to his people, and help him against his enemies.

precepts.text: Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon. Zion is the city of Judah, and the daughter of Babylon, when you read Psalms 137, is Edom. So Judah will be dwelling with Edom, living with his enemy.
precepts.point: Judah, thou art he whom thy brethren shall praise: thy hand shall be in the neck of thine enemies. Judah is going to be living in close proximity to his enemy, which today is Esau. Go back into the 60s and 70s: the Black Panthers, Martin Luther King, Malcolm X, a lot of movements where Judah rose up and was contending with the so-called white man. He couched as a lion, and as an old lion; who shall rouse him up? Christ is going to rouse him up.

note.label: Judgement! To Hell with Your Reparations!

precepts.why:
Jacob called his sons to tell them “that which shall befall you in the last days,” and of Judah he said, “thy hand shall be in the neck of thine enemies.” That says two things: Judah will be fighting his enemy, and Judah will be living in close proximity to his enemy, who today is Esau, Edom. Zechariah 2 is the scripture that proves Judah will be living with that enemy.

“Ho, ho, come forth, and flee from the land of the north, saith the Lord: for I have spread you abroad as the four winds of the heaven, saith the Lord.” Then: “Deliver thyself, O Zion, that dwellest with the daughter of Babylon.” Zion is the city of Judah. The daughter of Babylon, as Psalms 137 shows, is Edom, the Caucasian race. So Zion is dwelling with the daughter of Babylon: Judah living in the land of the north, in the house of his enemy.

That is the picture of Genesis 49:8. Judah’s hand in the neck of his enemies is Judah living with him and contending with him. In the 1960s and 70s there was the Black Panthers, Martin Luther King, Malcolm X, and many movements where Judah rose up and fought the so-called white man. “he stooped down, he couched as a lion,” and at one point it looked like he was about to strike.

But the lion lay back down: “as an old lion; who shall rouse him up?” Christ is the one who will rouse him up. Until then the word to Zion is to come forth and deliver himself from the daughter of Babylon he dwells with.

note.label: Puerto Rico: The Flame Of Resistance

precepts.why:
John saw one like unto the Son of man, and “his eyes were as a flame of fire.” That line tripped up Carlos, the host of the podcast The Theology of the Streets: was it literal, or figurative? So we go line upon line, to Genesis 49:12: “His eyes shall be red with wine.” When you drink wine, the whites of your eyes turn red. That is the flame of fire John saw. Christ drank wine, and Christ did not have blue eyes.

The same verse finishes, “and his teeth white with milk.” His teeth were white, and the milk has a meaning of its own, which 1 Peter 2:2 opens.

It fits the rest of the description. “His head and his hairs were white like wool, as white as snow”: that tells two things, the color and the texture. The color is white; the texture is wool, like the woolly hair of the negro, as some of the old dictionaries define woolly. Christ did not have blonde hair; he had an afro, white like wool. The pictures shown are not an exact image of Christ, but a more accurate depiction according to the scriptures.

This matters because our people say the image does not matter, as long as he is in my heart. But if you do not know what Christ looks like, you will be deceived and fall for the white man’s Jesus. Line upon line, here a little and there a little, is how the understanding comes, and it is not for everybody. If you are not keeping the commandments, or you go by what the Christian pastors teach, you will get lost.

precepts.text: Reuben's birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph because he defiled his father's bed.
precepts.point: Thou shalt not excel: Reuben would not excel as the firstborn, because he went up to his father's couch. His birthright was given unto the sons of Joseph because he defiled his father's bed, and the genealogy is not to be reckoned after the birthright.

note.label: Genesis 49: What Shall Befall the Twelve Tribes in the Last Days
